title: Pfizer, Verismo Strike Licensing Deals to Push CAR T Manufacturing In Vivo
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 18, 2026 Pfizer, Verismo Strike Licensing Deals to Push CAR T Manufacturing In Vivo Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Listen0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Verismo’s Pack-IT license supports in vivo engineering of KIR-CAR T cells, positioning the platform for off-the-shelf delivery with potential reductions in time-to-treatment, cost, and access barriers. Multi-chain KIR-CAR design aims to overcome single-chain CAR constraints, seeking durable antitumor activity with minimized off-target toxicity while Synkir-110 and Synkir-310 progress through Phase I. Pfizer secured ex-Greater China rights to three pre-IND in vivo CAR-T autoimmune programs from Starna, plus technology rights spanning inflammation/immunology and oncology, with options for additional compounds. Financial terms include $330 million upfront and up to $2.3 billion milestones plus royalties, while Pfizer controls ex-China clinical development, U.S. initial manufacturing, and commercialization. The transaction exemplifies large-pharma licensing of China-origin innovation after sustained national investment shifting from low-cost supply to advanced biopharma R&D.SHOW MORE Verismo Therapeutics licenses in vivo CAR T engineering technology from Stanford Medicine, while Pfizer licenses in vivo CAR-T programs from Starna Therapeutics. Advertisement A pair of licensing agreements this week pushed CAR T cell therapy into new territory, with two companies moving to engineer T cells directly inside the body rather than relying on today’s weeks-long manufacturing process.Verismo Therapeutics licenses in vivo CAR T technologyVerismo Therapeutics entered an agreement to license the Pack-it technology enabling in vivo engineering of KIR-CAR T cells from Stanford Medicine. The agreement provides Verismo with technology from the lab of Crystal Mackall, MD, Ernest and Amelia Gallo Family professor, professor of pediatrics and medicine at Stanford Medicine, and founding director of the Stanford Center for Cancer Cell Therapy.1The deal will allow Verismo to extend its multi-chain KIR-CAR platform into next-generation in vivo delivery of KIR-CAR T cell therapies, with the potential to reduce time-to-treatment and cost and broaden patient access over time.1 Verismo’s platform is designed to take CAR T therapy beyond the single-chain limitations of current approaches, with the potential to deliver durable anti-tumor responses while minimizing off-target toxicity. The platform is currently advancing in two Phase I clinical trials: Synkir-110 in solid tumors and Synkir-310 in B-cell malignancies.1 Both trials have generated early positive signals presented at the American Association for Cancer Research 2026 Annual Meeting. Kim continued, saying, "Today, KIR-CAR is advancing along the established CAR T pathway in two Phase 1 clinical trials, and adding the Pack-IT technology is intended to extend the platform into next-generation, off-the-shelf in vivo delivery, realizing the full potential of KIR-CAR to reach more patients, faster, and at lower cost."Pfizer licenses in vivo CAR-T programsPfizer entered into an exclusive licensing agreement with Starna Therapeutics under which Starna is set to receive an upfront payment of $330 million and is eligible for up to $2.3 billion in milestone payments tied to development and commercial milestones, plus royalties on net sales of approved products.2Under the agreement, Pfizer obtains exclusive rights outside Greater China to develop, manufacture and commercialize three pre-IND in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell programs focused on treating autoimmune diseases.2 Pfizer also receives rights to use Starna’s proprietary in vivo CAR-T technology in inflammation and immunology and in oncology, along with options to exclusively license compounds created under a separate research collaboration and an option to expand the territory to include exclusive rights to develop and commercialize each exclusively licensed compound and product in Greater China.2 Pfizer is expected to lead clinical development outside Greater China and plans to manufacture the finished drug product for the initial clinical trials using its facilities in the United States, with sole and exclusive control over commercialization outside Greater China for all products.The Pfizer-Starna deal also fits a broader pattern of large pharma licensing innovative technology out of China, as John Stanford, executive director at Incubate, told Pharmaceutical Executive, “the surge of interest in Chinese licensing is the product of two decades of deliberate investment. China had a very stated objective — not just to be a cheap supplier, but to edge into innovative industries. That investment is now paying off.”Michael Vincent, chief inflammation and immunology officer, Pfizer, says “In vivo CAR-T is an emerging and promising approach for treating autoimmune diseases, and the patients who might benefit most are those for whom today’s options fall short. Pfizer has significant experience in developing and manufacturing RNA-based medicines globally, and Starna’s in vivo CAR-T programs and technology give us a powerful way to pursue these approaches.”SourcesVerismo Therapeutics Licenses In Vivo CAR T Engineering Technology to Extend Its Novel Multi-Chain KIR-CAR Platform verismo Therapeutics November 18, 2026, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/verismo-therapeutics-licenses-in-vivo-car-t-engineering-technology-to-extend-its-novel-multi-chain-kir-car-platform-302943157.htmlPfizer Enters into Exclusive Licensing Agreement with Starna Therapeutics for Autoimmune Diseases Pfizer November 18, 2026, https://www.pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-enters-exclusive-licensing-agreement-starna Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. title: Gilead Signs Royalty-Free Licensing Deals to Broaden Access to Obeldesivir
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 17, 2026 Gilead Signs Royalty-Free Licensing Deals to Broaden Access to Obeldesivir Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Listen0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Royalty-free licenses authorize contingent manufacturing and distribution of obeldesivir within 127 countries, aligned with prior remdesivir COVID-19 licensing geographies and intended to compress timelines post-approval. Technology transfer planning has begun with three named manufacturers, and additional partners are being pursued to expand capacity before confirmatory clinical and regulatory milestones. The Ebo-pep Phase III randomized, placebo-controlled field trial is evaluating post-exposure prophylaxis efficacy in high-risk contacts during active outbreaks, coordinated by ALIMA and collaborators. Remdesivir has been donated for investigational/compassionate use in multiple countries, while separate WHO-sponsored Partners trial data may inform potential remdesivir labeling for Ebola BVD.SHOW MORE Gilead signs royalty-free licensing agreements with three generic manufacturers to expand future access to its investigational antiviral obeldesivir. Advertisement Gilead Sciences signed royalty-free voluntary licensing agreements with three generic manufacturers to support potential future access to its investigational antiviral obeldesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis for Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease.The agreements will cover 127 primarily low- and lower-middle-income countries, including all African countries that have reported cases during the current Ebola BVD outbreak.1 The move signals Gilead’s effort to get ahead of a currently ongoing outbreak by lining up manufacturing and supply capacity before clinical results are even in.The geographic scope of the new agreements mirrors Gilead’s existing voluntary licensing arrangements for remdesivir in Covid-19, with the agreements being designed to support manufacturing readiness, technology transfer, and supply planning, while a field trial evaluating obeldesivir continues.1What do the agreements cover?The royalty-free licenses allow Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma, and Ferozsons Laboratories to manufacture and supply obeldesivir in the licensed territory, contingent on clinical data and applicable regulatory authorizations.1 Technology transfer discussions are already underway with these three manufacturers, with Gilead saying agreements with additional manufacturers are under discussion. He continues to say, “These agreements reflect our commitment to preparing for future access while clinical research is ongoing, so that we are better positioned to respond if these investigational medicines demonstrate benefit and gain regulatory approval.”How has Gilead already responded to the outbreak?Beyond the new licensing agreements, Gilead has made direct product donations tied to the current outbreak. The company has donated more than 2,000 vials of remdesivir to Kenya for investigational use as treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis for people with confirmed Ebola BVD or individuals with a close contact exposure.1 More broadly, as part of its response to the current outbreak, Gilead has provided compassionate use donations of remdesivir to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and Kenya totaling more than 38,000 vials.These efforts sit within what Gilead describes as a broader approach to outbreak preparedness that includes clinical research, manufacturing and supply planning, technology transfer, and collaboration with governments, public health agencies and global health partners.The licensing announcement is one piece of a broader outbreak response. Gilead is also updating its existing voluntary licensing agreements for remdesivir to include filovirus disease, which would support potential future access should results from the ongoing World Health Organization-sponsored Partners trial support remdesivir’s use as a treatment for Ebola BVD, pending potential regulatory approvals.1 The clinical efficacy of remdesivir for the treatment of Ebola BVD has not been established, and remdesivir is not currently approved in any country for the treatment or prevention of the disease.SourcesGilead Expands Access to Investigational Obeldesivir for Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease Through Voluntary Licensing Gilead Sciences November 16, 2026, https://www.gilead.com/news/news-details/2026/gilead-expands-access-to-investigational-obeldesivir-for-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-through-voluntary-licensingFilovirus Post-Exposure Prophylaxis, preparedness and efficacy evaluation during outbreak in Central and West-Africa Global Health EDCTP3 August 1, 2026, https://www.global-health-edctp3.europa.eu/projects/ebo-pep-2026_en Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about Overton FDA nomination being yanked, a Merck setback, and more GSK lung cancer drug wins FDA approval, further validating its acquisition of Nuvalent Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanNov. 18, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the middle of the week. Congratulations on making it this far, and remember there are only a few more days until the weekend arrives. So keep plugging away. After all, what are the alternatives? While you ponder the possibilities, we invite you to join us for a needed cuppa stimulation. Our choice today is ginger peach turmeric. Meanwhile, here is the latest menu of tidbits to help you on your way. We hope you conquer the world and have a wonderful day. And as always, please do stay in touch. We appreciate feedback, tips, and criticism. … The Trump administration is pulling the nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the U.S. Food and Drug Administration over concerns that she lacked support to get confirmed by the Senate, STAT notes. The Senate’s health panel had been expected to vote on her nomination Wednesday, and the panel’s leader, Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), said on Tuesday that Overton had enough support to clear his committee and win confirmation. But some GOP lawmakers had reservations about Overton, a preventive care doctor who served in the Trump White House, due to her support for scaling back vaccine recommendations, her role in loosening restrictions on vapes, and her stance on abortion policy.Advertisement Merck plans to stop development of its experimental blood cancer drug, nemtabrutinib, after a ​review found the benefits may not outweigh the ‌risks, Reuters says. An independent monitoring committee reached that conclusion after reviewing results from a late-stage study and Merck said its review of the full ​data confirmed the finding. The decision ends a broader development program ​for treating chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma, ​including two other late-stage trials. Nemtabrutinib is an oral drug designed to block BTK, a ​protein that helps ​cancerous B ⁠cells grow. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account?
